pr_body:
This implements multiple Handle Value Notification (HVN) in one ATT_MULTIPLE_HANDLE_VALUE_NTF PDU. Core Spec 5 .3 | Vol 3, Part F, 3.4.7.4 section describes as this new PDU allows the GATT server to send the values of two or more attributes in a single PDU in the list of tuples of (handle, len, value). However, the Zephyr host currently supports multi HVN but it does not utilize the new ATT PDU of ATT_MULTIPLE_HANDLE_VALUE_NTF=0x23 fully. It is sending only one HVN per PDU, and it is no different from the existing regular single HVN with ATT_HANDLE_VALUE_NTF=0x1B.

Fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/40664

One thing to consider with this fix for the current implementation: When `bt_gatt_notify` is called, it will queue the notification immediately if it is a single notification. If `gatt_notify_mult` is called then it will be queued with a delay. That means we will have different behavior, depending on whether we are sending a mult-notification or not. 

For the majority of use cases, this is OK (typically we just want to send the notification and be done). However, for some services (unless that was changed since I last read the test specs) there is a specific order of things, i.e. some test specs mandates the order of operations to be

1. Client writes to characteristic A (CA)
2. Server notifies the new value of CA
3. Server send a write response

or 
1. Client writes to characteristic A (CA)
2. Server send a write response
3. Server notifies the new value of CA

i.e. the notifications will occasionally have to be sent before or after a write response (granted that in those cases the Test specs should probably support either order, unless specified by the service spec). Current we can control this when sending "regular" notifications, but if we do indeed postpone a notification (using the k_work approach) we won't ever be able to send the notification before the write response. 

It may not be a problem in the end, assuming that PTS and the test specs can deal with notifications coming in any order (w.r.t. write responses), but it is still something we need to consider (i.e. notify and mult-notify will behave differently if mult-notify uses k_work and notify does not).

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: GATT: EATT:  Multiple notify feature not utilize new PDU fully
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem?**
Bluetooth 5.2 introduced Multiple Handle Value Notification (HVN) sub-feature as part of Enhanced ATT feature.
Zephyr host currently supports multi HVN but it does not utilize new ATT PDU of `ATT_MULTIPLE_HANDLE_VALUE_NTF=0x23`  fully. It is sending only one HVN per PDU, and it is no different then existing regular single HVN with `ATT_HANDLE_VALUE_NTF=0x1B`.

Core Spec 5 .3 | Vol 3, Part F, 3.4.7.4 section describes as this new PDU allows to the GATT server to send the values of two or more attributes in a single PDU in the list of tuples of `(handle, len, value)`. So this new sub-feature should be supporting multiple HVN in one PDU.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Currently, Multiple HVN is sent with `bt_gatt_notify_multiple()` API that takes list of HVN info. But it is sending them in separate PDU iterating through them. Instead, it should be sent in single PDU as much as they fits.

review_comments: Alternatively, we could look into setting each `func` and `user_data` somehow

Indeed. All the individual `params` should have the callback invoked. But where do we store the whole list of `params`? We could..
 - ..add a `_internal.callback_chain` field to `struct bt_gatt_notify_params`. But then we again use the `params` struct to store temporary data, which as commented further up, is not great design.
 - ..require that the `bt_gatt_notify_params` are wrapped in a new struct specialized for multi-notifications.
 - ..somehow manage the storage for it in gatt.c.

@jori-nordic and I have concluded that it will be OK to keep this change and specify in the `bt_gatt_notify_multiple` API that all `params`'s `func` and `user_data` must be the same, and that there will be only one invocation of this callback per successful invocation of `bt_gatt_notify_multiple`. (This is like specifying the cb in the arguments of `bt_gatt_notify_multiple`, which may be a relevant future change to the API.)

The API change is less than it appears. Already before this change, consecutive notifications with the same callback `func` and `user_data` could have their callbacks merged at the stacks discretion. (Side note: That the stack was merging the callbacks without informing the application in any way is bad stuff.)

It is OK for me, as long as either create a TODO or a GH issue that documents the wish to improve this. 

My biggest worry with this API (which pretty much also existing beforehand), is that as an application, actually using the `bt_gatt_notify_multiple` instead of just calling `bt_gatt_notify` multiple time is so much more of a hassle, as well as being more limited that I do not have many intentions of actually using it as is (but at least we'll fix the issues the current implementation has).

yep agreed, the multiple api is a bit useless right now, I think we'll wait for actual use cases before reworking it, does that sound reasonable ? I'd like to get some feedback on how the users intend on using that feature, then we can make the necessary adjustments.
I know this is part of the existing solution, but I highly dislike updating the parameters like this (but no use fixing it just for notify_mult).

Yeah I recently encountered it in the gatt subscribed check, it was pretty misleading in gdb. I would be o.k. with either having a commit fixing this in the whole of gatt.c (As part of this PR) or merging it this way and then making a subsequent PR that fixes this kind of behavior.
I can draft that PR if you don't have the time @laxiLang , just tell me.

@jori-nordic Unfortunately I think this is a general issue in GATT. It's quite typical for GATT to modify the data in the parameter structs (for better or worse). 

It will be a significant API change to fix, so at this point the best course of action might be to add additional documentation about it.
@jori-nordic if you help with the proposal for a fix, do appreciate it.
@Thalley would you be ok merging this as-is (I mean this comment specifically) if I create a doc PR right after ? I don't want to add more noise to that one.
